steps: Claim or create a free Nextdoor Business Page for your local service business and verify it.
Complete your page: services, hours, photos, and contact info.
Get discovered in Nextdoor business search and neighborhood recommendations (Nextdoor notes over 25% of conversations are business recommendations).
Collect neighbor recommendations and respond to messages from locals asking for quotes.
Win the job and get paid directly by the customer on your own terms.
catches: Lead flow is inbound and reputation-based: it takes time to build recommendations, and there are no guaranteed leads.
You need a real local service business with a verifiable address; this is not a channel for remote/online-only freelancers.
The free path is organic only; paid placements (Local Deals ads) cost extra.
Results vary hugely by neighborhood density and how active your local Nextdoor community is.
Using a personal account to promote a business violates community norms and erodes trust.
biggest_catch: There are no guaranteed leads: Nextdoor is a slow-burn reputation channel, and a new page in a quiet neighborhood may produce nothing for months.
eligibility: Local businesses/service providers eligible under Nextdoor's Business Page Policy; must verify the business address.
timing: Always-on local discovery; jobs come in as neighbors search and ask for recommendations.

c1.evidence: Nextdoor's own help center states the mechanism: 'Local businesses can create Nextdoor Business Pages to connect with their neighbours. Through business pages, neighbours can leave a recommendation, message the business' and pages are free to create.

c2.evidence: Nextdoor publishes no payout terms — money comes from customers you win; framed as fully variable.

c3.evidence: Steps follow the official flow: create/claim free page, complete profile, get discovered, receive messages.

c4.evidence: Business Pages are free to create; no upfront fee documented for the organic path.

s1.note: Eligibility is local businesses under the Business Page Policy with a verifiable address.

s2.note: Framed as variable customer-paid work; no amount promised.

s3.note: Catches cover slow inbound flow, local-only fit, and no guaranteed leads.
